en: אִירָא m. (אור, compare חור) white substance, undyed wool or cotton. Shabbat 11ᵇ; (Tosefta ib. I, 8 missing). Ib. 79ᵃ דוגמא לא׳ a sample color for the wool (given to the dyer).—plural אִירִין. Bava Kamma 119ᵇ, the remnants of wool in the hands of the dyer. [R. Hanan. reads אִידָּא see as well] [Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra I, 4 אִירָה; Kelim XXI, 1 עִירָה.]

אַשְׁוָה, אַשְׁוָוה, (אַשְׁיָיָא, אַשְׁוָו׳) f. (שוי, compare אַשְׁיְתָא and אַשְׁוָתָא) skein, reel, clue, especially staff around which the wool is put, spool. Kelim XXI, 1 the wool which is on the distaff ובא׳ Arukh (ed. בא׳ correct accordingly) or on the spool. Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra I, 6 צמר שעל גבי האַשְׁוָוה ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant אשה, cler. err.).

חָלַך (compare חלל) to undermine, cave, dig. Pesachim 118ᵇ שחוֹלֶדֶת בעיקרי וכ׳ Manuscript Munich (ed. as in Chullin 20ᵇ הדרה) which undermines the foundations &c. V. חוּלְדָּה.

Hifil - הֶחְלִיד
1) same. Yerushalmi Kilayim IX, 32ᶜ top מַחִלִיד הב"ה … את וכ׳ the Lord caves the ground before them and they roll &c.; Yerushalmi Ketubot XII, 35ᵇ top מהלך … אל (correct accordingly). Bava Batra 19ᵇ מפני שמַחְלִידִין וכ׳ because their roots undermine the ground.

—2) to pass the slaughtering knife under cover, to squeeze in. Chullin II, 4. Ib. 20ᵇ; and from—Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra I, 5 מפני שהכובס אומן מַחֲלִידוֹ לתוכו (Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim XXI, 1) because so much of it does the professional fuller fold up for inserting a rod into it (see חוֹב II, 2).

כּוֹבֶד m. (Biblical Hebrew כֹּבֶד; כָּבֵר)
1) weight, heaviness, pressure. Sanhedrin 63ᵇ א"ת כבודו אלא כּוֹבְדוֹ Manuscript Munich, see כָּבֵד II. Yoma 41ᵇ בעי כ׳ it requires weight (must be heavy so as to sink into the fire). Ib. כדי שיהא בהן כ׳ (they are tied together) in order that they may be heavy. Yerushalmi Chagigah II, 77ᵈ צריך לכבוש את כּוֹבְדוֹ (in putting his hands on the sacrifice) he must press his weight on it; (Bavli ib. 16ᵇ סמיכה בכל בחו). Nazir 5ᵃ כ׳ the feeling of heaviness (of the hair).—כ׳ ראש bending down the head; humble, solemn disposition, opposed קלות ראש. Berakhot V, 1 אין עומדין … כ׳ ראש we must not rise for prayer in any other than a humble &c. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. I, 39ᵈ top; Tosefta Pirkei Avot Zar. I, 2 שואל בשלומו בכ׳ ר׳ greet him with a bent head (without ostentation). Moʿed Katan 21ᵇ בשפה רפה ובכ׳ ר׳ in an undertone and with solemnity.

—2) roller or beam of a loom; כ׳ העליון the upper beam from which the warp depends; כ׳ התחתון the lower beam, the roller on which the web is wound as it advances. Kelim XXI, 1 (Talmud ed. כֹּבֶד). Negaim XI, 9 (fem.). Shabbat 113ᵃ; Yerushalmi ib. XVII, 16ᵃ bottom of page

מַסֶּכֶת f. (Biblical Hebrew; סָכַךְ I)
1) web on the loom. Oholot VIII, 4 מ׳ הפרוסה the spread web, i.e. the web hanging from the transverse beam (vestis pendens, see Smith, Dictionary of Greek and Roman Antiquities, Third American Edition, New-York 1858 section (Parashah) see Tela). Kelim XXI, 1 נפש המ׳ the woof, opposed to שתי עומד the warp of the standing loom. Midrash Till. to Psalms XXXVIII; Yalkut Psalms 733 אנו המ׳ וכ׳ we are the web, and Thou the weaver; and e.

—2) (compare Lat. textus) construction, Talmudic treatise. Ruth Rabbah to II, 9 (play on וַיַּסֵּךְ, II Samuel XXIII, 16) עשאה מ׳ וקבעה וכ׳ (not מסכתא) he (David) constructed it and fixed it as a rule for future generations that the king forces the road &c. (see Sanhedrin II, 4); Midrash Samuel Chaldaic XX; Yerushalmi Sanhedrin II, 20ᶜ top. Shabbat 114ᵃ, see כַּלָּה; and from—plural מַסֶּכְתּוֹת. Midrash Till. to Psalms CIV, 25 אלו המ׳ דבר וכ׳ those are the systematic collections of Bar Ḳ. &c. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 18 ששים מ׳ sixty Talmudic treatises [editions, however, count sixty-three]; Midrash Tanḥuma Korah 12; Shir HaShirim Rabbah to VI, 9 (not … תיות); and from

נִיר IV m. (see preceding; compare jugum and ζυγόν, see Smith, Dictionary of Greek and Roman Antiquities, Third American Edition, New-York 1858 section (Parashah) see Tela) cross-beam of the loom, also the cross-rod under the cross-beam (liciatorium) to which the ends of the leashes are fastened; trnsf (mostly plural) נִירִים, נִירִין the leashes or thrums to which the threads of the warp are fastened; also the warp. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 94, see פָּתַל. Bava Kamma 119ᵇ אין לוקחין … ולא נ׳ you must not buy from the weaver remnants of woof or of warp threads. Kelim XXI, 1 הנוגע בנ׳ … he who touches the upper beam … or the rods, contradistinguished to קֵירוֹס.—בית נ׳ that portion of the web produced by passing the spool with the woof across the warp, mesh, slip. Shabbat XIII, 2 (105ᵃ) העושה שני בתי נ׳ בנִירַיִּים וכ׳ Manuscript Munich (ed. בנירין) he who starts a web by making two meshes, attaching them either to the cross-pieces or to the slips (קֵירוֹס). Ib. 105ᵃ ברוחב ג׳ בתי נ׳ within a distance of three meshes; (Tosefta ib. XII (XIII), 1 על ג׳ בתים). Yerushalmi ib. VII, 10ᶜ שני נ׳ בחף … בניר אחד two sets of warp threads fastened to one old border web (licium) or two borders fastened to one set of warp threads. Shekalim VIII, 5 על ע"ב נ׳ וכ׳ Manuscript Munich and Arukh (ed. נימין; see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l., p. לד, note) the curtain was woven on seventy-two leashes, and each twist of the warp (נִימָה) contained twenty four threads; Chullin 90ᵇ; Tamid 29ᵇ נימין; Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 4 נימין; Midrash Tanḥuma Vayaḳh. 7 נימין; ed. Bub. 10 נירים.

עִירָה f. (עָרָה II) thread on the shuttle used for the woof, bobbin. Kelim XXI, 1 ע׳ שאינו עתיד וכ׳ a bobbin which the weaver does not intend to shoot back again. Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra I, 4 אִירָה.—plural עִירִין. Bava Kamma 119ᵇ Arukh (ed. אִירִין, see Rashi and l.).—V. אִירָא.

comments.he: כל כלי אשר יעשה מלאכה בהם: כבר פירש זה (בסימן קיט). ופה מפרש מה שכתב "כל כלי" מלת "כל" בא לרבות כל שהיא כלי, אף הקלע והקמיע והתפלה. ומ"ש "אשר יעשה מלאכה בהם" דייק במה שכתב "יעשה" בנפעל – רק עלים נפעלים, לא פועלים מלאכה כמו העץ והעבות. ומתבאר במסכת כלים (משנה כלים פ"כא מ"א). ומ"ש מלת "בהם" – מדייק רק שנעשה המלאכה בהכלי עצמו, לא חפויי כלים שהמלאכה נעשה בהכלי והם רק מכסים הכלי שנעשה בו מלאכה.

comments.en: What is [the posture] of examining negaim? A man is inspected in the posture of one that hoes or one that gathers olives. And a woman [is inspected in the posture] of one who is arranging dough and one who nurses her child, and one that weaves at an upright loom if the nega was in the right armpit. Rabbi Judah says: also in the posture of one that spins flax if it was within the left armpit. Just as [is the posture] for examining for the nega, so too [is the posture] for shaving hair.
comments.he: כֵּיצַד רְאִיַּת הַנֶּגַע. הָאִישׁ נִרְאֶה כְעוֹדֵר, וּכְמוֹסֵק זֵיתִים. הָאִשָּׁה כְּעוֹרֶכֶת וּכְמֵנִיקָה אֶת בְּנָהּ, כְּאוֹרֶגֶת בְּעוֹמְדִין לַשֶּׁחִי לַיָּד הַיְמָנִית. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף כְּטוֹוָה בְפִשְׁתָּן לַשְּׂמָאלִית. כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּרְאֶה לְנִגְעוֹ, כָּךְ הוּא נִרְאֶה לְתִגְלַחְתּוֹ:

comments.en:
One who touches the vertical supports that are on either side [of the loom], or the vice that is on top of the [weaver's reeds, even though it is concave in shape and forms a [type of] receptacle, it is pure, and it can only become impure if it [directly] touches the iron. A menstruant who stretched out the rope and treaded on the reed that goes up and down (i.e., used for the vertical (warp) threads): The [woven] garment is impure [with midras-impurity (MS Vienna)].
It so happened that there was a certain woman who would weave garments in a state of purity, and she came before Rabbi Yishmael, and he was examining her. She said to him, "Rabbi, I know that this garment was not defiled, only that my heart was not [constantly] set on watching over it." During the examination that Rabbi Yishmael was performing on her, she said to him, "Rabbi, I know that a menstruant came in and stretched out the rope with me." Said Rabbi Yishmael, "How great are the words of the Sages, who said that one who does not intend to to watch over [an object], it is [deemed] impure!"
And there was another incident with a certain woman who would weave tablecloths in a state of purity, and she came before Rabbi Yishmael, and he was examining her. She said to him, "Rabbi, I know that this tablecloth was not defiled, just that my heart was not [constantly] set on watching over it." During the examination that Rabi Yishmael was performing on her, she said to him, "Rabbi I know that a thread broke and I knotted it in my mouth." Said Rabbi Yishmael, "How great are the words of the Sages, who said that one who does not intend to to watch over [an object], it is [deemed] impure!"
comments.he: הנוגע בעמודין שבצדדין מכאן ומכאן ובמכבש שעל גבי הקנים אע"פ שחקוק ומקבל טהור ואינו טמא אלא הנוגע בברזל לבד. נדה שמשכה את החבל ודרסה על הקנה העולה ויורד הבגד טמא מעשה באשה אחת שהיתה אורגת בגד בטהרה ובאת לפני ר' ישמעאל והיה בודקה אמרה לו רבי יודעת אני שלא נטמא הבגד אלא שלא היה בלבי לשומרו. מתוך בדיקות שהיה בודקה ר' ישמעאל אמרה לו רבי יודעת אני שנכנסה נדה ומשכה עמי בחבל א"ר ישמעאל כמה גדולים דברי חכמים שהיו אומרים לא נתכוון לשומרו טמא. שוב מעשה באשה אחת שהיתה אורגת מפה בטהרה ובאתה לפני ר' ישמעאל והיה בודקה אמרה לו רבי יודעת אני שלא נטמאת המפה אלא שלא היה בלבי לשומרה. מתוך בדיקות שהיה רבי ישמעאל בודקה אמרה לו רבי יודעת אני שנפסקה נימה וקשרתיה בפי א"ר ישמעאל כמה גדולים דברי חכמים שהיו אומרים אם לא נתכוון לשומרו טמא.

comments.en: And anything on which one of them falls when dead shall be unclean: be it any article of wood, or a cloth, or a skin, or a sack—any such article that can be put to use shall be dipped in water, and it shall remain unclean until evening; then it shall be clean.
comments.he: וְכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־יִפֹּל־עָלָיו֩ מֵהֶ֨ם ׀ בְּמֹתָ֜ם יִטְמָ֗א מִכׇּל־כְּלִי־עֵץ֙ א֣וֹ בֶ֤גֶד אוֹ־עוֹר֙ א֣וֹ שָׂ֔ק כׇּל־כְּלִ֕י אֲשֶׁר־יֵעָשֶׂ֥ה מְלָאכָ֖ה בָּהֶ֑ם בַּמַּ֧יִם יוּבָ֛א וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעֶ֖רֶב וְטָהֵֽר׃

comments.en: All at once, the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were crushed, and became like chaff of the threshing floors of summer; a wind carried them off until no trace of them was left. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
comments.he: בֵּאדַ֣יִן דָּ֣קוּ כַחֲדָ֡ה פַּרְזְלָא֩ חַסְפָּ֨א נְחָשָׁ֜א כַּסְפָּ֣א וְדַהֲבָ֗א וַהֲווֹ֙ כְּע֣וּר מִן־אִדְּרֵי־קַ֔יִט וּנְשָׂ֤א הִמּוֹן֙ רוּחָ֔א וְכׇל־אֲתַ֖ר לָא־הִשְׁתְּכַ֣ח לְה֑וֹן וְאַבְנָ֣א ׀ דִּֽי־מְחָ֣ת לְצַלְמָ֗א הֲוָ֛ת לְט֥וּר רַ֖ב וּמְלָ֥את כׇּל־אַרְעָֽא׃

sections.en: One who touches the upper beam, the lower beam, the harnesses, the sley, the thread that is drawn over purple material, or a spool which is not to be shot back, remains clean. If he touches the woof, the standing warp, the double thread that is drawn over purple material or a spool which is to be shot back, he becomes unclean. If one touches the wool that is on the distaff, or on the spool, he remains clean. If he touches the spinner: Before it was uncovered he is unclean, After it was uncovered he remains clean.
sections.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּכֹּבֶד הָעֶלְיוֹן, בַּכֹּבֶד הַתַּחְתּוֹן, בַּנִּירִים, וּבַקֵּירוֹס, וּבְחוּט שֶׁהֶעֱבִירוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי אַרְגָּמָן, וּבְעִירָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָתִיד לְהַחֲזִירָהּ, טָהוֹר. בְּנֶפֶשׁ הַמַּסֶּכֶת, וּבַשְּׁתִי הָעוֹמֵד, וּבְכָפוּל שֶׁהֶעֱבִירוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הָאַרְגָּמָן, וּבְעִירָה שֶׁהִיא עֲתִידָה לְהַחֲזִירָהּ, טָמֵא. הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּצֶּמֶר שֶׁעַל הָאִימָּה, בָּאַשְׁוָיָה, טָהוֹר. הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּפִּיקָה, עַד שֶׁלֹּא פֵרְעָהּ, טָמֵא. מִשֶּׁפֵּרְעָהּ, טָהוֹר:

en: *יָצוּל m. (יצל; compare אֵצֶל; see Wetzst. in Levy Talmud Dict. section (Parashah) see כורך) the cross-piece or handle of a plough. Kelim XXI, 2.
*כּוֹרֶךְ m. (כָּרַךְ; compare כְּרוּכָא) part of a plough containing a receptacle out of which the seed falls during the ploughing. Kelim XXI, 2 R. Hai G.; see, however, בֶּרֶךְ.

בֶּרֶךְ, (בּוֹרֶךְ) f. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding)
1) knee. Yerushalmi Berakhot I, 3ᵈ top.

—2) a knee-shaped pole. Taanit 25ᵇ כמלא ב׳ חמחרישה (Variant כוך, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l.) (until the rain penetrates) as far as the knee of the plough enters the soil; Oholot XVII, 1 בו׳. Kelim XXI, 2 בו׳. [Tosefta Sheviit IV, 20 ברך, see בְּרִיכָה.]—Dual בִּרְכַּיִם. Berakhot 34ᵇ; Megillah 22ᵇ; Shevuot 16ᵇ כריעה על ב׳ the word כרע means falling on one’s knees. [בִּרְכּוֹת, see בְּרִיכָה.]

חֶרֶב f. (Biblical Hebrew; compare חרף)
1) sword. Chullin 3ᵃ, see חָלָל I. Bava Batra 8ᵇ ח׳ קשה וכ׳ death in war is a greater affliction than natural death. Sanhedrin 116ᵃ מהם הרגו בח׳ some of them they put to death by the sword. Midrash Tanḥuma Balak 8; Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 20 אא"כ שלף חַרְבּוֹ without drawing his sword. Ib. בח׳ חייהם live on their sword. Taanit III, 5 על הח׳ on the sword, i.e. when armies are passing the country. Ib. 22ᵃ ח׳ של שלום a friendly army passing; and from

—2) the sword-shaped handle of a plough. Kelim XXI, 2. Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra I, 7.—plural חֲרָבוֹת. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 21 ח׳ מכאן וכ׳ (soldiers with) swords here &c.; and e.

מַסְוֶה m. (Biblical Hebrew; סוה , Ges. Thes., Ges. Thes. p. 941) cover, sheath; מ׳ שבמעדר the (iron) sheath of the ploughshare. Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra I, 7 (Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim XXI, 2 המ׳ שבמעצד). Eruvin 22ᵃ Manuscript Oxford, see מַשּוֹֹא.

סַתָּת m. (preceding) stone-cutter, chiseller. Yerushalmi Bava Metzia X, end, 12ᶜ, see סִיתּוּת; Bavli Bava Metzia 118ᵇ, חַצָּב; and from—Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 6 כלי הס׳ Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim XXI, 2 (ed. השַׂתָּת) the stone-cutter’s implements.—plural סַתָּתִים, סַתָּתִין. Kelim XXIX, 7. Yerushalmi Shekalim IV, 48ᵃ top; and e.

עֲבוֹת m. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding) chain, rope for fastening the yoke of the animal to the plough (Maimonides); [the pole tied to the yoke by means of a knotted rope (Rabbenu Shimshon)]. Kelim XXI, 2. Sifra Shʾmini, Parah 6, Chaldaic VIII.—Sanhedrin 99ᵇ (reference. to Isaiah V, 18) בתחלה … לע׳ העגלה at first the evil inclination resembles a thread of cobweb, and at the end it is like a wagon rope; Yalkut Breishit 129.—plural עֲבוֹתוֹת. Sukkah 52ᵃ; Yalkut Isaiah 270 (not עבותי׳).—V. עָבִית.
עֵירָאִין , Kelim XXI, 2 ed. Dehr., see עֵרָיִין

עֵרָיִין, עֵי׳, עֵירָאִין m. plural (עָרָה II) [stirrers,] iron-tipped ploughshare. Kelim XXI, 2; [Maim. ed. Dehr. = Arab. ʿalâḳath lorum, goad?]. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 6 עֲרָעִין (Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim l. common gender. ערערין).
קַטְרֵב m. a cross-piece in front of yoked animals; [oth. opinion, see Kohelet Arukh Compl. section (Parashah) see: the pin fastening the ropes of the yokes to the pole]. Kelim XIV, 4. Ib. XXI, 2.

comments.en:
I drew them with human ties,
With cords of love;
But I seemed to them as one
Who imposed a yoke on their jaws,
Though I was offering them food.
comments.he: בְּחַבְלֵ֨י אָדָ֤ם אֶמְשְׁכֵם֙ בַּעֲבֹת֣וֹת אַהֲבָ֔ה וָאֶהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם כִּמְרִ֥ימֵי עֹ֖ל עַ֣ל לְחֵיהֶ֑ם וְאַ֥ט אֵלָ֖יו אוֹכִֽיל׃

sections.en: One who touches the yoke, the crossbar, the collar-piece, or the thick ropes, even when they are being used, he remains clean. If he touched the tail piece, knee or handle, he becomes unclean. If he touched the metal rings, the guides, or the flanks, he becomes unclean. Rabbi Judah says that he remains clean if he touched the guides since they only serve to increase the soil.
sections.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּעֹל, וּבַקַּטְרָב, בָּעַיִן, וּבָעֲבוֹת, אֲפִלּוּ בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה, טָהוֹר. בַּחֶרֶב, וּבַבֹּרֶךְ, וּבַיָּצוּל, טָמֵא. בָּעַיִן שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, בַּלְּחָיַיִן, וּבָעֲרָיִין, טָמֵא. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר בַּלְּחָיַיִם, שֶׁאֵינָם עֲשׂוּיִן אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הֶעָפָר:

en:
אָשׁוּת Arukh, אֵישׁוּת ed. f. (Biblical Hebrew אֵשֶׁת Psalms LVIII, 9; אוש or אשש, see אשש
2) [groping, compare גוש, גשש,] mole. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 51 (alluding to esheth Psalms l. common gender.) כא׳ זו וכ׳ like that mole which sees not the light. Kelim XXI, 3 מצודת הא׳ the bow for shooting moles (see Maimonides and l.). Moʿed Katan I, 4; compare ib. 6ᵇ.—Yerushalmi ib. 80ᶜ, explained חולדה.

מְשִׁיחָה II f. (מָשַׁח II) band, cord, especially flax rope for surveying. Tosefta Eruvin VI (V), 13. Kelim XXI, 3 בחוט ובמ׳ the string or the rope (of the saw). Tosefta Shabbat V (VI), 2 כרכן במ׳ (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) במשיחא) tied a cord around them; Shabbat 50ᵃ. Tosefta Chullin III (IV), 22 כל הנותן ע"ג מ׳ החולק וכ׳ when you place a fowl on a rope, that fowl which divides its claws &c., is unclean; Chullin 65ᵃ מותחין לו חוט של מ׳ you stretch a cord for it in a line; and from—plural מְשִׁיחוֹת. Kilayim IX, 9 מ׳ של ארגמן purple-colored ribbons, see מָלַל I end; Yerushalmi ib. 32ᵈ. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 7.

מְצוּדָה f. (Biblical Hebrew; צוּד) hunting apparatus, net, trap; bow. Kelim XXI, 3, see אָשׁוּת. Ib. XV, 6 מְצוּדַת החולדה a trap for weasels. Shabbat 43ᵇ שלא יעשנה כמ׳ he must not spread the mat so as to form a trap (for the bees). Esther Rabbah to III, 2 (reference. to Psalms CXL, 6) מ׳ פרשו לי או"ה וכ׳ the nations laid a trap to ruin me, saying to me, worship idols &c. Pirkei Avot III, 16 מ׳ פרוסה על וכ׳ a net is spread over all the living (none can escape divine judgment); and e.—Berakhot 9ᵇ; Pesachim 119ᵃ כמ׳ זו שאין בה דגים Manuscript Munich (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 30) like a net without fish; (oth. version כמ׳ … דגן like a fort without provision; Rashi: like a trap without grain to attract the birds), see מְצוּלָה.—plural מְצוּדוֹת. Tosefta Beitzah III, 1; Yerushalmi Shabbat XIII, 14ᵃ bottom of page; Yerushalmi Beitzah III, 62ᵃ top מְצָדוֹת; and from—[Yerushalmi Eruvin IV, 21ᵈ bottom of page מצודות, read: מְצוֹפוֹת.]

מַסָּר m. (Biblical Hebrew מַשּׂוֹר; נָסַר) a tool with rough edges or teeth, file, saw. Shabbat XVII, 4 מ׳ הגדול saw for cutting wood. Kelim XXI, 3; Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra I, 8 מלבן של מ׳ הגדול the frame of the saw. Yerushalmi Sukkah III, 53ᶜ bottom of page כמין מ׳ leaves serrated like a saw, see מַגָּל; Tosefta Sukkah II, 7; Bavli Sukkah 34ᵃ דומה למ׳. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 6; Midrash Samuel Chaldaic IX, see נָסַר; Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 5 כס׳ (Variant כמַסְמָר); and e.

מָתַח (Biblical Hebrew) to extend, stretch (compare משך, משח). Kilayim VI, 9 המוֹתֵחַ זמורה וכ׳ if one trains a vine from one tree to another. Shabbat 75ᵃ המותח חוט וכ׳ he who pulls the thread of a seam (bringing the ends closer together), see infra. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 3, and e. שלא תאמר מיכאל היה מותח וכ׳ lest you say, Michael stretched (the world) in the south &c., see מָדַד; Midrash Till. to Psalms XXIV מְמַתֵּחַ. Yerushalmi Berakhot I, 2ᵈ top אדם מותח אהל וכ׳ when one stretches a tent-cover, in course of time it becomes loose; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 12, end; Yalkut Isaiah 314.—Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 10, end, see Nifal—[Yalkut Mishlei 961 סופו להיות מותח see מָתַק.]—Part. pass. מָתוּחַ; f. מְתוּחָה; plural מְתוּחִים, מְתוּחִין; מְתוּחוֹת stretched, extended; (of a bow) bent; trnsf. (of judgment) ready to be discharged, aimed. Kelim XXI, 3. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 35 אותה מדת הדין שהיתה מ׳ כנגד … ומְתָחָהּ וכ׳ that very judgment which was aimed against Israel, did the Lord turn and aim against the Egyptians. Yerushalmi Moʿed Katan III, 83ᶜ top הדין מ׳ כנגד וכ׳ judgment is ready against the whole family. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 38; and from

Piël - מִיתֵּחַ same, especially to straiten straps; to bring objects closer together. Moʿed Katan I, 8 אף מְמַתְּהִין you may also straigten (bed-straps). Ib. 10ᵃ וממתחין שאם … מְמַתְּחוֹ ‘you may stretch’, means when it (a strap) is lax, you may straiten it; Yerushalmi ib. I, 80ᵈ bottom of page Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra IV, 10 מחוסרין … למַתֵּחַ need … stretching. Midrash Till. l. common gender., see supra.—Yerushalmi Shabbat XIII, beginning 14ᵃ המְמַתֵּחַ צדדין (ed. Krot. הממחה צדדיו, correct accordingly) he who brings the ends of two pieces close together (by pulling the thread up and knotting it), see supra; Yerushalmi Kilayim IX, end, 32ᵈ המְמַתֵּיחַ צדדין (or המַמְתִּיחַ Hifil; not צדדיו); and e.

Nifal - נִמְתַּח to be stretched, spread, drawn. Sanhedrin 38ᵇ נִמְתְּחוּ אבריו his limbs were stretched (shaped); (Pirkei Avot d’ R. N. Chaldaic I נתקשרו); Yalkut Breishit 15. Ib. 16 היו נִמְתָּחִין והולכין (ib. also מוֹתְחִין; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 10, end מותחין) they (the works of creation) continued to extend (develop). Yerushalmi Berakhot I, 2ᶜ bottom of page יִמָּתֵחַ הרקיע (or יִמְתַּח) let the firmament be stretched out. Rosh Hashanah 22ᵇ יִמָּתֵחַ על העמוד shall be stretched on the pillory. Yerushalmi Horayot II, 46ᵈ נִמְתְּחָה הקשת the bow was bent (euphem. for erection). Yalkut Psalms 796 נמתחה החרב the sword (of judgment) was drawn; (Midrash Tanḥuma B’midb. 7 נמשכה; ib. ed. Bub. 7 נשמטה).

Hithpaël - הִתְמַתֵּחַ same. Midrash Tanḥuma Ḥayé 3 והיו הולכין ומִתְמַתְּחִין וכ׳ they would have gone on spreading &c.

סָנִיף m. (סָנַף) attachment, wedge; key-stone. Midrash Till. to Psalms XCI; Pirké d’R. El. Chaldaic XXXV; Yalkut Breishit 120 כאדם שהוא נותן ס׳ לכיפה as one inserts a key-stone in an arch. Berakhot 47ᵇ; Yerushalmi ib. VI, 11ᵇ top עושין אותו ס׳ לעשרה we wedge him in among the ten, i.e. we count him in so as to make up the requisite number; and from—plural סְנִיפִים, סְנִיפִין. Tosefta Sanhedrin VII, 9 בבית … עושין אותן ס׳ at a wedding feast we place them among (the adults); Horayot 13ᵇ. Taanit 25ᵃ ס׳ עשאום they made them (the beams) in links, i.e. joined mortised pieces to them. Tosefta Menachot XI, 6 ארבע ס׳ … היו וכ׳ four golden attachments were there (to the table) shaped like forks; Menachot XI, 6. Ib. 94ᵇ והס׳ מעמידין וכ׳ and these attachments supported the loaves; Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 4; and from—Kelim XXI, 3 ס׳ the side-pieces of a saw which hold the blade, and the wedge with which the cord is twisted

קַשְׁטָנִית f. (preceding article) bow-shaped handle of a borer, ‘bow-drill’ (see Smith, Dictionary of Greek and Roman Antiquities, Third American Edition, New-York 18583 section (Parashah) see Terebra). Kelim XXI, 3 (ed. Dehr. קוּשְׁטָ׳). Tosefta Shabbat XIII (XIV), 17 מטלטלין את הקשט׳ Arukh (ed. הקַשְׁתָּ׳) you may handle the bow-drill (on the Sabbath); ולא יקדיח בק׳ וכ׳ but you must not bore (a wine cask &c.) as you do on week days.

comments.en:
A weasel that dragged a shuttle thread, which he intended to weave back in, and brought [the thread] into a house with a corpse inside of it: Even though there was only a minute amount [of material] inside the tent [covering the corpse], the garment is defiled with corpse-impurity. [If] a zav treaded on it within ten handbreadths, the garment is defiled with midras-impurity. The warp: As long as he intends to weave [on it], it is [considered] connected to whatever is woven [on it]. [If] he finished weaving, it is only impure up until the place that he intends to separate [the unused threads]. One who touches the separated threads of the warp or of the woof, behold, that is not considered connected. Rabbi Yosei says, one who touches the separated threads of the warp up to three fingers' [breadth], it is connected, for the fuller is an expert at pleating [loose threads] back into [the garment]. One who touches the wool which is on the spool, or the spun wool that is on the whirl of the spindle, it is pure, but [if it is] on the spindle [itself] or on the vertical supports [of the loom], it is impure. One who touches the black [wool] that is on top of [other] black [wool], it is pure, but if everything on one side was black, and he moved it on top of the white [on the other side], or [if] everything on one side was white, and he moved it on top of the black, it is impure.
The [sword-shaped] handle of a plough that became detached along with the peg of a plough, behold, it is impure, because he digs circular trenches around wells with it. The eye of the axe and the eye of the plough and the sheath of the ploughshare: Whenever they are attached, they are considered connected for purposes of impurity and for sprinkling [the waters of purification], [and] whenever they are by themselves, they are pure. The threads and straps that are on the share-beam: If they are sewn, they are considered connected, and if they are knotted, they are not considered connected.
A carpenter's vice: Whenever it is attached, it is considered connected for purposes of impurity and sprinkling. [If] it is removed, it is not considered connected, either for impurity or for sprinkling. Rabbi Yehuda says, even one who touches the frame of a large saw on either side remains pure, and only contracts impurity in the place where it is held by hand, on either side facing the iron [of the saw].
comments.he: חולדה שגררה את העירה שהוא עתיד להחזירה והכניסתו לבית שהמת בתוכו אע"פ שאין באהל אלא כל שהוא הבגד טמא טמא מת. דרס עליה הזב בתוך י' טפחים הבגד טמא מדרס. שתי כל זמן שהוא עתיד לארוג חבור לאריג. גמר מלארוג אינו טמא אלא עד מקום שהוא עתיד לפצוע. הנוגע בפסיקות של שתי ושל ערב הרי זה אינו חבור. ר' יוסי אומר הנוגע בפסיקות של שתי עד ג' אצבעות חבור מפני שחבובים אומן מחלידו לתוכו. הנוגע בצמר שעל גבי האומה ובטווי <שעל גבי הפלך> טהור ובכוש ובעומד טמא. נוגע בשחור שעל גבי השחור טהור אבל אם היה כולו שחור מצד אחד והעבירו ע"ג לבן או כולו לבן מצד אחד והעבירו על גבי שחור טמא. החרב שפירשה עם יתדות המחרישה הרי זו טמאה מפני שהוא מנקר בה חוליות של באר העיין שבמעצד והעיין שבמחרישה והמסוה שבמעדר בזמן שהן קבועין חבור לטומאה ולהזאה. בזמן שהן בפני עצמן טהורין. המשיחות והרצועות שבמעדר תפורות חבור וקשורות אין חבור. מכבש של נגר בזמן שהוא קבוע חבור לטומאה ולהזאה. ניטל אין חבור לא לטומאה ולא להזאה רבי יהודה אומר אף הנוגע במלבן של מסר הגדול מכאן ומכאן טהור ואינו טמא אלא מקום החיות יד מכאן ומכאן כלפי הברזל.

sections.en: One who touches the handle of a saw at either end becomes unclean; [If he touched] its string, cord, cross-piece or side-pieces, a carpenter's vice, or the bow-handle of a bow-drill, he remains clean. Rabbi Judah says: so too he who touches the frame of a large saw remains clean. One who touches the bow-string or the bow, even though it was stretched, he remains clean. A mole-trap is clean. Rabbi Judah says: when it is stretched, the separate parts are [regarded as] connected.
sections.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּיַד מְגֵרָה, מִכָּאן וּמִכָּאן, טָמֵא. בַּחוּט, וּבַמְּשִׁיחָה, בָּאַמָּה, וּבַסְּנִיפִין, בַּמַּכְבֵּשׁ שֶׁל חָרָשׁ, וּבַקַּשְׁטָנִית, טָהוֹר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּמַּלְבֵּן שֶׁל מַסָּר הַגָּדוֹל, טָהוֹר. הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּיֶּתֶר וּבַקֶּשֶׁת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא מְתוּחָה, טָהוֹר. מְצֻדַּת הָאֵישׁוּת, טְהוֹרָה. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהִיא מְתוּחָה, חִבּוּר:
